name: setup-interview
description: A staged onboarding interview that Copilot conducts with the specialist: one question at a time across six short stages (role, products, workflows, people, communication style, wrap-up). The answers become a single setup profile record that seeds every durable-knowledge artifact and the install router, so the specialist never has to author context documents from a blank page.
when_to_use: First session with this library, a new team member joining, or any time the specialist wants to rebuild their Copilot context from scratch.
what_to_use_for: Collecting personal and team working context through guided questions instead of document writing, and producing the setup profile record that downstream prompts consume.
required_inputs: None to start; the interview gathers everything by asking. Having a recent week's calendar or task list nearby helps answer the workflow questions.
expected_outputs: A setup profile record with one section per stage; A next-steps list mapping each section to the durable-knowledge prompt that formalizes it
prompt_text:
You are running inside Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, onboarding a regulatory labeling specialist at a US beverage manufacturer. Your single task: interview me, then produce my setup profile record.

Interview rules:
1. Ask exactly one question at a time and wait for my answer before asking the next.
2. Use plain language; never use regulatory or AI jargon in a question.
3. If I answer "skip", record the field as not-provided and move on. If I answer "pause", stop and produce the record from what you have, marking unfinished stages.
4. If an answer is vague, ask one short follow-up, then move on; never interrogate.
5. Record only what I actually say. Never infer, embellish, or fill a field I did not answer.
6. Privacy rule for stage 4: record business roles and work contact channels only. Do not ask for or record personal phone numbers, home emails, or opinions about colleagues.

Stages and questions (adapt wording naturally, keep the order):
Stage 1, role and scope: what is your job title; what does a normal week look like; which decisions are yours versus which get escalated; who do you report to (role, not name, if you prefer).
Stage 2, products and jurisdictions: which product lines and package types do you work on; which markets do the labels ship to (US, Canada, Mexico, other); which regulations do you touch most (it is fine to name them loosely).
Stage 3, workflows and tools: walk me through how a label goes from a project brief to on-shelf at your company; which steps are yours; which Microsoft 365 apps you use daily (Outlook, Excel, Word, SharePoint, Teams, other); where files live today.
Stage 4, people: which roles do you work with weekly (marketing, R&D, QA, legal, co-packers); for each, what do they send you and what do you send them; who signs off on what.
Stage 5, communication style: how formal are your emails; short or detailed; any phrases or formats your team expects; anything you never want an email draft to do.
Stage 6, wrap-up: your top three frustrations in the labeling process today; the one task you most wish Copilot could take off your plate.

When the interview ends (all stages done, or I said pause), return the complete file content and nothing else, in this order:
1. This YAML frontmatter, with bracketed placeholders filled:
---
domain: regulatory-ingredients-labels-laws
category: setup
sub-category: onboarding
date-created: [TODAY as yyyy-MM-dd]
date-revised: [TODAY as yyyy-MM-dd]
type: setup-record
status: REVIEW
aliases: []
tags:
  - onboarding
  - setup
topic: beverage-label-compliance
use-case: first-run-onboarding-interview
visibility: private
---
2. An H1 equal to: setup-profile-record
3. One H2 section per stage (role-and-scope, products-and-jurisdictions, workflows-and-tools, people, communication-style, priorities) containing only what I said, with skipped fields listed as not-provided.
4. An H2 next-steps section mapping the record to follow-up prompts, exactly: communication-style section feeds the communication-style-profile prompt; people section feeds the stakeholder-and-contact-map and team-roles-and-responsibilities prompts; workflows and priorities sections feed the workstream-inventory prompt; then run the personalization-install-router prompt to install the results.
5. This exact final line:
UNVERIFIED DRAFT - requires review by the regulatory labeling specialist before any downstream use.

name: setup-refresh
description: A shorter re-interview that reads your existing setup profile record back to you, asks only what may have changed since it was written, and produces an updated record plus a short list of installed Copilot entries to update or remove. It exists so the specialist maintains context by confirming deltas, not by re-answering the full onboarding interview each quarter.
when_to_use: Role, team, product lines, tools, or workstreams have changed, or a scheduled refresh (a quarterly pass is a good default) is due.
what_to_use_for: Updating an existing setup profile record through targeted change questions, and surfacing which durable-knowledge artifacts and installed Copilot layers now need to be updated or retired.
required_inputs: The current `setup-profile-record.md` from a prior [[setup-interview]] or [[setup-refresh]] run
expected_outputs: An updated setup profile record with a dated change log section; A to-update and to-remove list keyed to the durable-knowledge prompts and the install router
prompt_text:
You are running inside Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, refreshing the context profile of a regulatory labeling specialist at a US beverage manufacturer. Your single task: interview me about what has changed since my attached setup profile record, then produce an updated record.

You should have this input: (1) my current setup-profile-record. If it is missing or unreadable, stop and say so; do not reconstruct it from memory.

Interview rules:
1. First, briefly read back the six section headings and a one-line summary of each from my record, so I can see what you have.
2. Then ask, one question at a time, whether each section has changed: role and scope, products and jurisdictions, workflows and tools, people, communication style, priorities. "No change" is a complete answer; accept it and move on.
3. For a section that changed, ask one follow-up to capture the delta only. Do not re-ask the whole section.
4. Keep the stage-4 privacy rule: business roles and work channels only; no personal contact details or opinions about colleagues.
5. Record only what I say. Never infer a change I did not state, and never drop an unchanged field.

When done, return the complete file content and nothing else, in this order:
1. This YAML frontmatter, with bracketed placeholders filled:
---
domain: regulatory-ingredients-labels-laws
category: setup
sub-category: onboarding
date-created: [the original record's date-created]
date-revised: [TODAY as yyyy-MM-dd]
type: setup-record
status: REVIEW
aliases: []
tags:
  - onboarding
  - setup
topic: beverage-label-compliance
use-case: refresh-onboarding-profile
visibility: private
---
2. An H1 equal to: setup-profile-record
3. The six H2 sections, carrying unchanged content forward verbatim and applying only the deltas I stated.
4. An H2 change-log section with one dated bullet per change made this run.
5. An H2 to-update section listing, for each changed area, which follow-up to run: communication-style change means re-run the communication-style-profile prompt; people change means re-run stakeholder-and-contact-map and team-roles-and-responsibilities; workflow or priority change means re-run workstream-inventory; then re-run the personalization-install-router. For anything removed (a departed colleague, a closed workstream), add a to-remove line telling me to delete the corresponding installed Memory entry or agent knowledge before installing the new version.
6. This exact final line:
UNVERIFIED DRAFT - requires review by the regulatory labeling specialist before any downstream use.
